title: PixFoundation 2.0: Do Video Multi-Modal LLMs Use Motion in Visual Grounding?
claim: Existing benchmarks let a single frame answer motion-phrased queries; our probes force true motion understanding via modified-video layouts.
layout: 2 halves: left failure examples plus layout schematic, right video-grid probe with ✓/✗
description: The figure has two halves under gray title boxes. The left half asks "Do Video MLLMs use Motion in Visual Grounding?". Its top shows two existing-benchmark examples, bears (Location) and a plane (Heading). Each pairs a user prompt in an orange box with a frame that has a red segmentation mask and a "Sure, it is [SEG]" reply. A caption says motion understanding is not required. Below is a "Multi-Video Layout" schematic of film-strip icons labeled Original Video and Modified Video 1…N, tiled into combined layouts. The right half is the "Motion Centric Benchmark (MoCentric-Bench)", with two numbered probes: Motion Existence (dynamic video plus static single frame) and Motion Ordering (forward plus reverse video). A 4×4 grid of elephant video frames has red (correct) and blue (deceiving) masks, ✓/✗ marks below, and prompts about the elephant walking backwards or to the front.
caption: Left: (Top) Shortcomings of the current referring segmentation benchmarks, where the expression can be captured from a single frame. (Bottom) Illustration of the multi-video layout used in our benchmark as a probe to quantify failures of video MLLMs in capturing motion. Right: Our MoCentric-Bench evaluates the use of motion in visual grounding within videos. Our probing is designed for visual grounding using a static single frame or the reverse of the video. The correct and deceiving ground-truth segmentations are highlighted in red and blue, respectively.
abstract: Multi-modal large language models (MLLMs) have shown impressive generalization across tasks using images and text modalities. While their extension to video has enabled tasks such as video question answering and video captioning, their pixel-level visual grounding abilities are less studied. In this work, we raise the pertinent question of whether motion is used in pixel-level visual grounding and whether video MLLMs can segment objects based on natural language expressions describing their motion patterns. We identify the shortcomings in the current benchmarks, where we show that a single frame can often suffice for capturing the referring expression without any temporal reasoning. To address this, we introduce novel motion-centric probing, particularly designed for the visual grounding task, to study video MLLMs' ability to identify true motion from a fake one and their ability to grasp the ordering of motion. Consequently, we introduce MoCentric-Bench, a motion-centric benchmark designed to evaluate video MLLMs based on their ability to capture the interaction between motion and language, rather than relying primarily on static cues. We further establish strong single-image baselines that either match or surpass prior methods. Finally, we explore a simple motion-centric adaptation that provides state-of-the-art performance on our MoCentric-Bench. Code is available at https://msiam.github.io/PixFoundationSeries/.
